pages.title: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content

claims.claim: Using automation, including AI, to generate content with the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings is a violation of Google's spam policies.
claims.quote: to generate content with the primary purpose of manipulating ranking in search results is a violation of our spam policies.

claims.claim: Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against Google's guidelines; not all use of automation, including AI generation, is spam.
claims.quote: Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines.

claims.claim: Using AI gives content no special ranking gains; content that is useful, helpful, original and satisfies aspects of E-E-A-T might do well in Search.
claims.quote: Using AI doesn't give content any special gains. It's just content.

claims.claim: Google uses a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to identify spam content however it is produced.
claims.quote: We have a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to help us identify spam content, however it is produced.

claims.claim: Google says AI disclosures are useful where readers might ask how content was created, and that giving AI an author byline is probably not the best approach.
claims.quote: Giving AI an author byline is probably not the best way to follow our recommendation to make clear to readers when AI is part of the content creation process.
